newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM aluminium up in buoyant trade helped by LME.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM aluminium up in buoyant trade helped by LME.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures finished higher in buoyant trade on Friday as the metal powered ahead on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
"Aluminium's fairly strong on the LME. And it seems we don't have to worry about a possible decline in the dollar," said one trader "People feel its safe to buy the contracts."
Traders also said individual investors had started to pay more attention to Tokyo aluminium futures as the metal looked set to move out and up from its recent trading range.
The June contract was up 1.8 yen at 198.8 yen per kg and the April added 2.8 yen to end at 200.4.
Others were up between 1.6 and 2.3 yen.
In London overnight, where zinc climbed to a new seven-year high, three month aluminium clawed up $12 to end at $1,654 per tonne, well above resistance at $1,650.
The cash/threes contango fell to $4/$2 from $17/$15, reflecting tightness in the market.
